The JUUL product consists of two main components: e-liquid and the JUUL device. JUUL e-liquid aims to provide a nicotine experience similar to combustible cigarette use. As smokers for many years,  they could find no acceptable alternative. Adam and James recognized an opportunity to apply industrial design to the tobacco industry. The result was the JUUL product.Our commitmentWe understand that trust in our company and category has eroded with our stakeholders and it is our responsibility to earn back that trust through our actions. To earn a license to operate in society, we are putting stakeholder trust at the center of what we do and make choices that are informed by the views of our stakeholders, including and especially our regulators.Our intentOur customer base is the world’s one billion adult smokers. We do not want any non-nicotine users, especially those underage, to try our products as they exist only to transition the world’s one billion adult smokers away from combustible cigarettes. We believe smokers should first and foremost quit. But for those who cannot or will not quit, access to alternatives to combustible cigarettes and accurate information about those alternatives is critical.

basic_info.name: QSENSE - PRIN 2022
basic_info.description: QSENSE is a PRIN 2022 project, funded by the Italian Ministry MUR, gathering an interdisciplinary team of experts in the fields of photonics, materials science, computational physics and spectroscopic sensing from three research units: Politecnico di Milano, Università degli Studi Roma Tre and Università di Pisa, in collaboration with Sapienza Università di Roma.The QSENSE project targets the demonstration of novel architectures for photonics integrated circuits (PIC) sensing chips operating in the Mid-infrared (MIR), where molecules display their unique spectral fingerprints, fabricated from SiGe layers epitaxially grown on a Si wafer. The chips will then host waveguides with an optical sensing region, where the analytes will interact with the evanescent filed of the guided mode, and an integrated quantum well infrared photodetector (QWIP). The final goal is the development of a sensing platform for the detection of the spectral fingerprint of a large class of analytes, including methane (CH4). Nevertheless, the impact of the proposed technology is not limited to environmental monitoring but can promote disruptive advances also in healthcare and safety & security, by replacing bulky, expensive, sophisticated MIR spectroscopy systems.
